problem.headline: Organizations that fail to scale technologically
problem.description: They have systems that were never designed to grow. The same patterns show up in data, in operations, and in AI initiatives — and they all share the same root cause.

dataChaos.title: Data that can't be used to make decisions
dataChaos.description: Not because it doesn't exist — but because it lives fragmented, ungoverned, in tools that don't talk to each other. Every department works from its own version of the numbers.
dataChaos.consequence: When there's no shared source of truth, meetings replace decisions and trust in the data erodes with every contradictory report.

inefficientProcesses.title: Processes that depend on people, not systems
inefficientProcesses.description: Manual workflows, Excel reports, operations that only work because someone knows how to run them. When that knowledge never makes it into a system, scaling becomes impossible.
inefficientProcesses.consequence: Operational risk grows with every undocumented process. What works today because someone is holding it together becomes tomorrow's most expensive point of failure.

uncertainFuture.title: AI initiatives that never reach production
uncertainFuture.description: Not for lack of ambition — but because the infrastructure behind them was never ready. AI projects that fail almost always fail before a single line of model code is written.
uncertainFuture.consequence: They fail in the data, in the processes, in the architecture. AI isn't the problem — it's the mirror that reflects everything that should have been built first.

results.headline: Real projects.
results.description: This is how we turn scattered data and manual processes into systems that actually reach production.

aiAgentsSwarm.headline: From scattered marketing tasks to a coordinated swarm of AI agents
aiAgentsSwarm.quote: Cabana Data cut the time a marketing team spends pulling together campaign history from 20 minutes to 2, by implementing a swarm of 8 specialized AI agents on top of LangChain.
aiAgentsSwarm.summary: The account management, strategy, media, creative, design, and digital platform management teams relied on manual, disconnected processes to research campaigns, define audiences, write copy, produce visual concepts, and put together presentations — each task in a different tool, with no shared memory. We implemented a master AI Agent overseeing 8 specialized subagents built on LangChain, which interprets the user's request and automatically delegates it to the right specialist.

excelToBigquery.headline: How we automated report generation and saved 40 hours/month in data analysis
excelToBigquery.quote: Cabana Data eliminated 40 hours a week of manual reporting work for a digital advertising client, automating 45 entities across 8 different platforms in Google BigQuery.
excelToBigquery.summary: A client with a significant presence in digital advertising faced a critical bottleneck: their reporting was built on metrics platforms → spreadsheets with hundreds of formulas → visualization tools. Reports would crash, filters took up to 4 minutes to run, and the formulas became unmanageable. We designed a custom data architecture and implemented a robust layer of automated flows and transformations in Google BigQuery, completely replacing the manual logic.

salesQuotaVisibility.headline: Real-time sales quota visibility with scalable transactional architecture
salesQuotaVisibility.quote: Cabana Data built a sales quota tracking platform that meets 98.6% of the client's cybersecurity checklist, consolidating 3 data sources into a single model.
salesQuotaVisibility.summary: This company needed to consolidate quota progress, sales targets, and commitment tracking into a single platform. We built a custom full-stack application (Angular + NestJS + BigQuery) with integrated SSO authentication, syncing data daily and powering real-time reporting for agents, supervisors, and managers. The result: hierarchical visibility into goal completion and an audited system that meets 98.6% of the client's cybersecurity checklist.

whatServices.question: What data services does Cabana Data offer?
whatServices.answer: We offer 4 service lines: Data Consulting (diagnosis and use case definition), Data Engineering and Architecture (infrastructure, pipelines, and Machine Learning), Custom Applications and Dashboards (digital products and visual analytics), and AI and Intelligent Systems (AI maturity diagnosis and custom agents). Each can be engaged independently, depending on where your organization stands.

projectDuration.question: How long does a typical data engineering project take?
projectDuration.answer: It varies by scope — whether it's just architecture and pipelines, or also includes a Machine Learning component. We define it precisely after understanding your data sources and goals, usually in the first conversation.

cloudPlatforms.question: Do you work with cloud platforms like AWS, GCP, and Azure?
cloudPlatforms.answer: Google Cloud is our standard platform for every project, with real hands-on experience in AWS as well for clients already operating there. We also have specific knowledge of Microsoft Fabric for clients with data initiatives already built on that ecosystem, though it's not our standard for application deployment.

industries.question: What industries do you serve?
industries.answer: We work with mid-sized companies in Costa Rica and LATAM across sectors like financial services, retail/CPG, marketing agencies, and logistics — organizations that need technology that works in production, not just in presentations.

security.question: How do you ensure data security and compliance?
security.answer: We apply strong technical security practices on every project — access control, anonymization of sensitive data at the source, row-level security on dashboards. We don't offer legal compliance consulting (GDPR, local regulations); we recommend that this assessment be handled by a specialized legal advisor in parallel with our technical work.

quality.title: Data quality and integrity
quality.question: Is your data reliable, complete, and consistent?
quality.description: We assess the coverage, completeness, and consistency of your data sources. We identify duplication issues, null values, and discrepancies between systems that affect the quality of any AI model.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure and pipelines
infrastructure.question: Does your architecture support AI workloads in production?
infrastructure.description: We review your data stack: storage, orchestration, latency, and scalability. An AI model in production requires reliable pipelines and infrastructure that can handle variable demand.

governance.title: Governance and privacy
governance.question: Do you control who accesses your data and how it's used?
governance.description: We audit access controls, retention policies, regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, local laws), and the traceability mechanisms that support ethical and secure data use.

maturity.title: Process maturity
maturity.question: Are your processes documented and reproducible?
maturity.description: We analyze the level of documentation, automation, and reproducibility of your workflows. Manual, undocumented processes are one of the biggest obstacles to scaling AI.

strategy.title: AI strategy and use cases
strategy.question: Do they know what they want AI for — and have the budget to execute it?
strategy.description: We assess whether there's a clear vision of priority use cases, defined success criteria, and alignment between the technical team and the business to prioritize and fund AI initiatives.

talent.title: Talent and organizational capacity
talent.question: Who's going to operate, maintain, and evolve this?
talent.description: We map the current team's capabilities, knowledge gaps, and the organizational structure needed to sustain AI operations in production long term.

whyNotBuild.question: Why can't we just start building directly?
whyNotBuild.answer: You could — and sometimes that's the right call. But if you've never diagnosed your infrastructure or prioritized use cases, building without that clarity almost always ends up solving the wrong problem, or building something no one in the business ends up using.

genericConsulting.question: Is this the same as generic "digital transformation" consulting?
genericConsulting.answer: No. We don't deliver a PDF of abstract recommendations. DHC delivers an objective score across 6 dimensions with evidence, not opinion. DUC delivers a DUC-CARD for each use case, with a prioritized roadmap and technical path. Both are anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, the international data management standard — not an improvised framework.

bothServices.question: Do we need to do both services (DHC and DUC), or just one?
bothServices.answer: It depends on where you stand. If you already know your infrastructure is solid and just need to define what to build, you can go straight to DUC. If you're not sure about your data foundation, we start with DHC. We define it together in the first conversation — not before.

howInvasive.question: How invasive is the process for our team?
howInvasive.answer: We work through scheduled interviews and workshops, not permanent access to critical systems. The time we ask of your stakeholders is limited and scheduled in advance.

notReady.question: What happens if the diagnosis shows we're not ready for what we wanted to do?
notReady.answer: We tell you directly, without softening it. We'd rather tell you the truth about the real blockers than let you move forward into a project that's going to fail because the foundation wasn't ready.

cost.question: How much does it cost?
cost.answer: It's quoted based on your organization's specific scope — we don't have a single list price. What we can give you on the first call is clarity on which path (DHC, DUC, or both) makes sense for your case.

caseStudy.headline: How we automated report generation and saved 40 hours/week in data analysis
caseStudy.summary: A client with a significant presence in digital advertising faced a critical bottleneck: their reporting was built on advertising campaign metrics platforms → spreadsheets with hundreds of formulas → visualization tools (Power BI and Google Data Studio). Every day, the incremental sync of advertising campaign data added more complexity. Reports would crash, filters took up to 4 minutes to run, and the formulas became unmanageable, generating constant errors that compromised data reliability. We conducted a thorough inventory of every data source, designed a data architecture tailored to the organization, and implemented a robust layer of automated flows and transformations in Google BigQuery. The solution completely replaced the spreadsheets' manual logic with reliable, auditable data pipelines.

personalytics.title: Building a One-of-a-Kind Media Planning Platform
personalytics.description: We designed the data architecture and reactive pipelines behind Personalytics — giving London Media a proprietary planning product powered by unified, real-time audience intelligence.

clientOverview.description1: London Media is a full-service media agency specialized in data-driven campaign planning and audience segmentation for brands across Latin America. With a growing client base and increasingly complex data requirements, they needed a unified platform to centralize media performance data and power smarter planning decisions.
clientOverview.description2: Personalytics is their proprietary media planning tool — built from the ground up alongside Cabana Data to turn raw audience and performance signals into actionable planning intelligence.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.p1: London Media operated with multiple disconnected data sources — ad platforms, CRM tools, spreadsheet exports, and third-party audience providers. Campaign planners spent hours manually consolidating data before any meaningful analysis could begin.
challenge.p2: The lack of a unified data layer made it impossible to build a reliable, real-time planning product. Personalytics needed a solid data foundation before a single feature could launch.
challenge.p3: The team needed a partner who could design the data architecture from scratch, integrate heterogeneous sources, and deliver a reactive pipeline capable of powering a product used daily by media planners.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.description: Instead of patching the existing chaos, we built the data infrastructure Personalytics needed to be a world-class product.
approach.step1Description: We mapped every data source London Media relied on — ad platforms, audience providers, CRM exports — and defined a consolidation strategy that eliminated silos without disrupting existing workflows.
approach.step2Description: We designed a cloud-native data pipeline on Google BigQuery, ingesting real-time and batch data from more than 8 sources into a unified semantic layer that Personalytics could query reliably.
approach.step3Description: With clean, structured data in place, we modeled the audience and performance entities that power planning intelligence — giving media planners the signals they need, when they need them.

results.title: Results That Made a Difference
results.stat1Description: Unify more than 8 fragmented data sources into a single, queryable layer that powers all of Personalytics' planning functions.
results.stat2Description: Reduction in time spent manually consolidating data — from days to hours, freeing planners to focus on strategy.
results.stat3Description: Audience and performance signals now flow reactively into Personalytics, enabling live campaign adjustments with no engineering bottlenecks.

impact.title: Transformative
impact.description: Beyond the technical delivery, this project redefined how London Media operates — and opened up a new product category in the media planning space.
impact.impact1: Personalytics launched as a fully functional product, with a data layer capable of scaling to thousands of campaigns.
impact.impact2: Media planners cut manual data work by 95%, moving from spreadsheet consolidation to real-time interaction with the platform.
impact.impact3: London Media gained a proprietary competitive edge — a planning product no competitor offers in their market.
impact.impact4: The pipeline architecture now supports multi-client deployments, turning a one-off project into a scalable product line.
impact.impact5: Data governance and lineage were established from day one, laying the groundwork for future AI and ML capabilities.

takeaway.title: Key Takeaway
takeaway.p1: Personalytics didn't just need a dashboard — it needed a data product mindset applied end to end. By treating the data layer as a first-class product component, London Media was able to launch faster, scale smarter, and compete at a fundamentally different level.
takeaway.p2: The lesson is universal: before you can build smart products, you need smart data infrastructure. That's what Cabana Data delivers.
takeaway.highlight1: A product is only as good as its data foundation.
takeaway.highlight2: Reactive pipelines turn static reports into living intelligence.
takeaway.highlight3: Data architecture is a product decision, not a backend detail.
